items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Simeon, myself, Don Kirkpatrick, Freddie Moore, we all sit there and listened. And they went through the whole thing. 'Well, you left Mama when we needed you. We was on the road, and you left us and went to school.'

ctx.x: argument, and Wilbur went on... They almost come to blows. And then after that, everybody stopped. Simeon, myself, Don Kirkpatrick, Freddie Moore, we all sit there and listened. And they went through the whole thing. "Well, you left Mama when we needed you. We was on the road, and you left us and went to school." On and on like that.
They took you all through that, huh.

Now, there was another broadcast that's been put out apparently on the label called Kings Of Jazz. It was recorded in New York here on the 24th of May, 1947. It's got Sidney Bechet, Wild Bill Davidson, George Brunis on trombone and apparently singing, Albert Nicholas on clarinet, James P. Johnson is on piano, Danny Barker is playing the banjo, Pops Foster, and then yourself. The three selections that are on this release include "Wildcat Blues," "Ain't Misbehavin'" and "Blue Turning Gray Over You." Do you remember…
Maybe so, but I don't remember. I don't remember what the (?) at that time...
